title: How do we find 55 squared from a square of side 60?
description: Two strips are cut from a square of side sixty to leave a square of side fifty five. The corner that was cut twice is added back. Keeko doubts that taking away five squared is enough.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square of side a minus b is the big square, less two strips, plus the corner that was cut twice. Watch for students who take away only b squared and leave the two strips in.

source: Find 55² from the square of side 60.
video_script.why: The child has cut a square into two squares and two rectangles. Here a smaller square is made by cutting strips away from a bigger one.
video_script.substitution: Start with the big square, cut away the two strips, and add back the corner that was cut twice.
video_script.anchor: a square of side sixty with two strips of width five cut away
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes away five squared from sixty squared and gets three thousand five hundred seventy five. That removes only the small corner, so the two strips are still counted and the area is too big.
video_script.payoff_line: A corner cut twice must be added back once

final_answer.spoken: fifty five squared is three thousand twenty five

maths_rules: the 5 by 5 corner was cut twice, so add 5² = 25 back once
taking away only 5² from 60² gives 3600 − 25 = 3575, which leaves both strips counted
video_script.design: One idea: cut two strips from a big square and add back the corner that was cut twice. Uses the cut square from the square of a sum. Wrong idea: take away five squared. The picture stays on the board through the doubt.
